text: I was a second year student and took LSD with my roommate in our dorm. We had done it once before and it was fun. This time, maybe two hours in, I was looking out the window at the night sky and I suddenly understood that the universe is going to end. Not in a scientific way, but I felt it, the heat death, all the stars going out one by one, and nothing left, forever. And that everything I do, everyone I love, all of it is just a tiny flicker before the endless dark. My roommate was laughing at something on his laptop and it seemed obscene to me that he could laugh. I sat on the floor with my back against the bed and couldn't stop thinking about infinity. It felt like my mind was being stretched beyond what it could hold. I asked him if he ever thought about how nothing matters, and he said 'dude you're just tripping' and put on some music. I spent the rest of the night staring at the wall feeling an indescribable dread.

Auf einem Festival habe ich 2C-B genommen und später noch Ketamin. Ich hatte plötzlich keinen Körper mehr und dachte, ich hätte mich aufgelöst. Ich hatte Angst, dass ich nicht zurückkomme, aber nach einer Stunde war es vorbei.

Some context first. I'm a veteran, two deployments to Afghanistan, and I was diagnosed with PTSD after I got out. I'd heard about MDMA and psilocybin trials for veterans and I was on a waiting list for one, but the wait was over a year and I was in a bad place. A buddy from my unit knew a guy who did underground sessions and I decided to go.

The guy who ran it seemed okay at first. He had a room set up in his basement with a mattress, blankets, candles, and a speaker. He said he'd been trained by people who'd worked on the trials. In the intake he asked me about my trauma and I told him the basics. We did MDMA first and then about 90 minutes later a dose of mushrooms. He said this combination would 'open the heart and then open the mind'.

The MDMA part was actually good. For the first time in years I felt safe and warm, and I talked about some of the things I'd seen over there. I cried, he listened. Then the mushrooms kicked in and it all went sideways.

The candles turned into muzzle flashes. The speaker was playing some kind of tribal drumming and it sounded exactly like rounds hitting the vehicle. I was back in the ambush. I mean really back, not remembering it, being there. I could smell the dust and the burning rubber and I could hear my guys yelling. I saw my friend who died that day, and he was looking right at me, and his face was the way it was when we pulled him out. I knew we were taking fire from the left. I tried to get to cover.

I don't remember everything after that. The guy running it told me later that I flipped the mattress over and got behind it and started yelling commands, and when he came close to calm me down I grabbed him and threw him into the wall. He hit his head and was bleeding. I don't remember doing that. What I remember is that at some point I wasn't in Afghanistan anymore but I wasn't in the basement either. I was nowhere, there was no me, no body, no time, just pieces of memory flying around like shrapnel. I didn't know which parts were me. I felt like I was being torn apart and every piece was screaming.

When I came back a bit, I was sitting in the corner and the guy was on the phone. I heard him say he didn't know what to do. I thought he was calling in an airstrike on my position. I got up and ran out of the house. It was night, raining, and I ran through the neighbourhood barefoot until I found a park and hid under a slide. I don't know how long I was there. Someone saw me and called the police. When they arrived with their lights I thought it was the enemy and I tried to fight them too. They tased me. I remember the pain and then the ground.

I spent the night in a holding cell and was taken to a VA hospital the next morning. I was still not right. I didn't know what had happened to the guy in the basement and I was terrified I'd killed him. It turned out he had a concussion and a cut on his head. He didn't press charges, I think because he didn't want anyone to know what he was doing. I was charged with resisting arrest, which was later dropped after my lawyer explained my PTSD.

The whole thing lasted maybe 7 or 8 hours. The worst part, beyond all of it, was that I had hurt someone. That's the thing I was most afraid of since coming home, that I'd lose control and hurt someone, and it happened.
Bad trip with lsd, saw my face melt in the mirror and felt like I'm losing my mind.

Ich war auf einer WG-Party, wir hatten Pilze gegessen, ich ungefähr 3,5 Gramm, viel mehr als sonst. Am Anfang fühlte ich mich unglaublich mächtig, als würde ich alles verstehen. Ich hatte das Gefühl, eine Art Gott zu sein, der die Welt erschaffen hat. Ich habe den anderen erzählt, dass ich jetzt die Wahrheit kenne, und alle haben gelacht. Dann kippte es. Wenn ich Gott bin, dann bin ich allein. Es gibt niemanden außer mir, alle anderen sind nur Figuren, die ich mir ausgedacht habe. Diese Einsamkeit war das Schrecklichste, was ich je gefühlt habe. Ich habe mich aufgelöst, es gab nur noch dieses unendliche Bewusstsein, das für immer allein ist. Ich wollte zurück, aber es gab kein Zurück, weil es kein Ich mehr gab, zu dem ich zurück konnte. Ich lag auf dem Boden im Flur und habe geweint, und die anderen sind über mich hinweggestiegen, weil sie dachten, ich mache Spaß. Eine Mitbewohnerin hat sich dann zu mir gesetzt und mich gefragt, ob alles okay ist, und ich habe sie angestarrt und nicht gewusst, ob sie existiert. Erst gegen Morgen kam ich langsam zurück in meinen Körper.

I attended a ceremony with a religious group in Brazil that uses ayahuasca as a sacrament. I went with a friend who was a member. I didn't know how strict it would be. Men and women sat on separate sides, everyone in white, and we had to stand and sing hymns for hours in Portuguese, which I didn't speak. We weren't allowed to leave the room except to purge, and then a 'guardian' would accompany you and bring you back.

The brew was very strong. After an hour I started seeing snakes, hundreds of them, coming out of the floor and the walls. They wrapped around my legs and climbed up my body. I felt them in my mouth. I wanted to scream but you weren't supposed to make noise. I tried to sit down and a guardian came and lifted me back up and told me to stay firm in the current. I felt like I was in hell, and that I'd been brought there for my sins, and the singing was the voice of judgement. I lost track of who I was. I just knew I was being punished and that it would never end.

At some point I vomited and the guardian took me outside. In the bathroom I collapsed on the floor and couldn't get up. I heard the hymns through the wall for what felt like a whole night. When I finally came back to the hall I stood at the back, shaking, until it was over. Nobody asked me how I was. My friend said afterwards it was 'a strong work' and that it meant I had a lot to clean. I flew home two days later.

Ich mache seit einer Weile Microdosing mit Pilzen. An einem Morgen habe ich offenbar die Kapseln verwechselt und eine viel zu hohe Dosis genommen, bevor ich ins Büro gefahren bin. Nach einer Stunde im Meeting merkte ich, dass etwas nicht stimmt. Die Gesichter meiner Kollegen begannen sich zu verziehen, und ich hatte das Gefühl, dass alle wissen, was los ist, und mich beobachten. Ich habe mich auf der Toilette eingeschlossen und gewartet, bis es vorbei ist. Ich hatte panische Angst, dass jemand es merkt und ich meinen Job verliere.

Someone passed me a DMT vape at a house party and I took a big hit without really knowing what it was. I broke through and found myself in a room made of shifting machinery. There were small beings, bouncing and chattering, and they showed me that the world I came from was a simulation they had built. They laughed at me for believing it was real. Then they turned me inside out. I could see the code behind everything, and my own life was just a loop running in that code. When I came back to the party, I didn't believe anyone was real. I looked at my friends and they seemed like NPCs. I left and walked home alone, trying to find a glitch that would prove it.

A group of four of us went to the desert in Arizona to take peyote buttons that one of my friends had been given by someone. It was summer, which in hindsight was idiotic. We started in the late morning. The taste was horrible and I threw up twice in the first hour, which I had been told was normal. By noon it was over 40 degrees and there was almost no shade. I started to feel the peyote but also the heat, and they became the same thing. My skin was burning, my head was pounding, and I felt like the sun was a giant eye staring into me.
I lost track of my friends. I think I wandered off to find shade. I sat under a rock overhang and the rock started to breathe. I saw faces in the rock, old faces, and I felt that they were my ancestors and that they were telling me it was time to come with them. I believed I was dying, and part of me accepted it. I remember thinking that this was a peaceful way to go. But then my body panicked, my heart was beating so fast I could feel it in my eyes, and I couldn't get enough air. I tried to stand and fell.
My friends found me about two hours later. One of them had water and they poured it over me and made me drink. They had to half-carry me back to the car and then drive two hours to a town with a clinic. I was diagnosed with heat exhaustion and severe dehydration. I was lucky.
LSD mit Leuten, die ich kaum kannte, die Stimmung in der Gruppe war schlecht und aggressiv. Ich hatte Angst, verrückt zu werden, und konnte nicht weg.

I drank ayahuasca at a small ceremony in Costa Rica. I purged a lot and then I saw my brother, who died of an overdose five years ago. He looked healthy and calm. He hugged me and I felt his love. It was overwhelming, I sobbed for hours. It was challenging because the grief I had been holding came up all at once, and for a while I couldn't breathe from crying.

Ich habe an einem Psilocybin-Retreat in den Niederlanden teilgenommen. Ich hatte vorher eine Absicht formuliert: Ich wollte meine Beziehung zu meiner Mutter verstehen. Schon nach kurzer Zeit kamen Bilder aus meiner Kindheit. Ich sah mich als kleines Mädchen, allein in meinem Zimmer, während meine Mutter im Nebenzimmer trank und schrie. Ich spürte die ganze Angst und Einsamkeit von damals in meinem Körper. Ich habe am ganzen Körper gezittert und laut geweint. Die Begleiterin war offensichtlich überfordert, sie hat mir nur gesagt, ich solle atmen, und ist dann zu anderen Teilnehmern gegangen. Ich lag da und hatte das Gefühl, wieder ganz allein zu sein, genau wie damals. Das hat es noch schlimmer gemacht. Gegen Ende der Erfahrung wurde es ruhiger, und ich hatte einen kurzen Moment von Mitgefühl mit dem kleinen Mädchen. Aber die meiste Zeit war es einfach nur schmerzhaft.
